evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese Character Database, CUHK）
evidence.field: 字形演變、構形爭議及早期用例
evidence.text: The database reports oracle-bone 多 as formed from two 肉 shapes. It describes later bronze and bamboo-slip components as visually confused with 夕, while noting a bronze 宜 component that preserves a 肉-like shape. It presents two accounts of the graph’s motivation: two pieces of meat conveying abundance (attributed to 季旭昇), and duplication analogous to 林, while citing a one-meat personal-name variant as counterevidence. It concludes that the original motivation is unclear. It reports early inscriptional 多 meaning ‘many’, including 《合集》12496 多雨 and 不其簋 多禽（擒）, and cites 多言後 from a Warring States bamboo text as an adverbial/frequentative use. The page does not date each cited artifact or demonstrate a complete semantic pathway.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly database reporting paleographic analyses and primary-text attestations
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 肉部字形及「多」相關條目

evidence.source: 《殷虚卜辞综述》引卜辞来源研究 PDF
evidence.text: The inspected table lists 《合集》12496 with the transcription 今一月多雨 and also lists other corpus references for 多雨. This corroborates an oracle-bone context for ‘many rain’; the table provides corpus identifiers but does not independently establish a calendar date for the individual inscription.
evidence.kind: scholarly reference table to primary oracle-bone inscriptions
evidence.title: 殷虚卜辞综述与甲骨文合集对照表

evidence.text: The page describes the cited oracle-bone corpus as Late Shang inscriptions, broadly ca. 1554–1045/40 BCE, and says the extant Shang divination inscriptions discussed come from Wu Ding and successors, around 1200 BCE. This supplies broad context for the oracle-bone medium, not an exact date for 《合集》12496.
evidence.title: Oracle-Bone Inscriptions of the Late Shang Dynasty

evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen explanation glosses 多 as ‘重也’ and analyzes it as 重 plus 夕, with 夕 explained through 相繹. This is an early lexicographic analysis and should not be treated as independent proof of the graph’s original form or motivation.
evidence.title: 說文解字 : 卷八 : 多部

evidence.source: Kotobank, citing Heibonsha 普及版 字通
evidence.text: 字通 analyzes the graph as 夕 plus 夕, with 夕 representing 肉, and explains 多 as abundant meat. It lists senses including ‘many’, ‘surpass’, ‘excess’, and ‘praise/esteem’, and reports older gloss traditions. This is a dictionary account; the inspected CUHK discussion leaves the earliest motivation unresolved, and these listed senses do not by themselves establish their chronology or semantic links.
evidence.title: コトバンク — 普及版 字通「多」

evidence.source: 文音聲韻查詢系統, reporting 廣韻
evidence.text: The entry reports 多 as 得何切, 端母, 歌一韻, 平聲. This is a Middle Chinese rhyme-book classification; the page does not provide evidence of a phonetic component within 多.
evidence.title: 「多」字的廣韻切語及中古讀音

evidence.source: 小學堂字形演變資料庫 — Academia Sinica
evidence.field: 字形演變、解形與 rights status
evidence.text: The inspected page displays labeled categories for oracle-bone, bronze, Chu bamboo/silk, small-seal and Shuowen forms and repeats competing explanations of two 夕 components versus 夕 as meat. Its footer states All Rights Reserved. No asset from this site is proposed for reuse; the official Xiaoxuetang single-character query returned HTTP 401 in the supplied query result.
evidence.title: 漢字「多」：字形演變

evidence.field: File description, source provenance and license
evidence.text: The file page identifies 多-oracle.svg as a depiction of 多 in Shang oracle script style, says its source references include the Academia Sinica database and Hanziyuan, and points to Hanziyuan record J16735 for this drawing. The file is a modern Inkscape SVG redraw, not an artifact photograph. Its page states a public-domain release for the SVG representation. The original-file endpoint was identified on the page but the web tool failed to fetch the image binary.
evidence.title: File:多-oracle.svg

evidence.field: Original file URL and access result
evidence.text: The Commons file page links the original SVG at this URL; opening it failed with a cache-miss error. The page itself was inspected and supplied the file identity and rights statement, but this research did not inspect the rendered pixels.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Shuowen text and a Guangyun-based phonological entry. These confirm the historical lexicographic account and reported Middle Chinese classification, not an original component sound role.

gaps: The earliest graph’s motivation remains unsettled in the inspected paleographic account: the two-meat and duplication analyses are proposals, and a one-meat personal-name variant complicates them.

The proposed transition from early 肉-like forms to later forms visually read as 夕 is supported as a reported graphic development, but no dated sequence or precise point of graphic conflation was established here. The transmitted Shuowen account of 重夕 is a separate historical explanation.

The early ‘many’ sense is supported by oracle-bone contexts including 《合集》12496, but no exact date for that individual inscription was established. The broadly Late Shang corpus dating is contextual only. The cited Warring States adverbial use does not establish a full semantic chronology.

Dictionary-listed extensions such as ‘surpass’, ‘excess’, and ‘praise/esteem’ were not traced to dated attestations or linked through a documented semantic pathway. No full chronology should be inferred from the gloss list.

No sound component or whole-graph phonetic loan claim was substantiated. Modern Mandarin and Guangyun evidence are available, but no component role is independently proposed, so there is no second character reading to compare phonologically.
The Xiaoxuetang per-character query was unavailable (HTTP 401 in supplied query data), and its rights notice page did not expose readable text during inspection. No Xiaoxuetang image was selected.

The proposed Commons glyph is documented and its modern redraw and public-domain status are described on the source page, but the direct file binary could not be fetched in this research stage; its pixels were not inspected.

items.period: Shang oracle script style; file page does not specify a narrower date
items.caption: A modern redraw of an oracle-script form of 多. A consulted paleographic account reports early 多 forms analyzed as two 肉 shapes, while the original graph’s motivation remains disputed.
items.alt: Modern vector drawing identified by its Commons page as 多 in Shang oracle script style.
items.selection_reason: The file page identifies the character and script style, supplies provenance to Hanziyuan record J16735 and reuse rights, and the form is relevant to the reported early two-肉 analysis. It is a redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph; pixels were not inspected in this research stage.
items.rights: Public domain release for the SVG representation, as stated on the Commons file page.

limitations.text: This candidate is a modern redraw of an ancient script form, not a photograph or rubbing of an excavated oracle bone. The file page supplies its identity and rights statement, but the linked binary could not be fetched here and the image pixels were not visually inspected.

The file’s oracle-script label alone does not prove whether its depicted component should be interpreted as 肉 or 夕; that graphic analysis is reported separately by the paleographic database, which itself regards original motivation as unresolved.
